subject: Service affinity fallback & customer opt-in for impacted regions
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@vectorhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Latency spike in US-east / fallback options

Marcus —

We're seeing sustained tail latency (95th ~ 1.7s) for text-generation calls originating in our US-east region since 07:40 PDT. The issue is intermittent but affecting live feature traffic. Our engineering on-call (eng-oncall@vectorhealth.com) has traced it to increased token service latency when requests route to a subset of hosts.

Can Redwood advise a safe way for us to opt our tenant into a cross-region fallback (prefer us->us-west or eu depending on capacity) while preserving context and KV cache where possible? We want to avoid a sudden model switch that would change outputs for active sessions.

Also: we need logs for 07:30–08:45 and any guidance on temporary TTL changes for cached prefixes.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Jenkins
Head of ML Platform, VectorHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@vectorhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Latency spike in US-east / fallback options

Team — forwarding VectorHealth. High priority customer experiencing increased token latency in us-east. Sara is explicitly requesting a controlled opt-in to a fallback path that preserves session continuity (no model variant swap unless necessary). Two asks: (1) Can infra prepare a playbook we can send that toggles "service-affinity fallback" for the tenant (route-by-affinity -> alternate-region) and warms KV cache in the target region? (2) Can we produce the logs for 07:30–08:45 and a short recommended TTL adjustment for prefix caching?

Proposed immediate steps: Neha -> routing/fallback instructions and safe roll procedure; Vanessa -> confirm capacity in us-west/eu for VH; Ben -> commercial note if any SLA/credits required. I'll coordinate with Sara on timing.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@vectorhealth.com>, eng-oncall@vectorhealth.com
Date: 2026-09-21T08:49:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Latency spike in US-east / fallback options

Marcus / Sara —

Quick triage summary: we observed increased token service latency tied to a localized host pool in us-east; control-plane was healthy. We can enable a tenant-level affinity fallback that routes new sessions to an alternate region while continuing to honor existing KV cache bindings for active sessions for a configurable grace window. Key points and safe steps (short):

1) Opt-in mechanism (non-disruptive): update tenant routing preference via API PATCH /tenants/{id}/routing with payload {"affinityFallback":"enabled","fallbackRegions":["us-west-2","eu-west-1"],"graceWindowSeconds":600}. This will only affect newly created session tokens; active sessions continue against original hosts for graceWindowSeconds.

2) KV cache warmup: run the warmup job to populate prefix cache in target region. Command: POST /ops/warmup?tenant=VH&target=us-west-2 with the attached kv-cache-checklist.csv. Warmup should be started BEFORE toggling routing to avoid cold-cache penalties. Expected warmup time 3–10 minutes depending on prefix size.

3) Model parity: We will NOT change model variant during this operation. If capacity constraints force a variant downgrade we will flag the session and notify.

4) TTL guidance: temporarily increase prefix TTL from default 60s -> 300s for 15 minutes while fallbacks stabilize. See attached kv-cache-checklist.csv for exact endpoints.

5) Logs: attached incident-logs-20260921.zip contains request traces (trace ids obfuscated per policy) covering 07:30–08:45. If you need raw traces we will provide secure link.

6) Rollback: revert PATCH to routing to disable affinityFallback. If we detect increased error rates post-fallback we'll auto-revert after 5 minutes unless manually confirmed.

Attachments: reroute_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook steps), kv-cache-checklist.csv, incident-logs-20260921.zip

I'll run warmup on approval and coordinate with Vanessa for capacity checks.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Infrastructure Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@vectorhealth.com>, eng-oncall@vectorhealth.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike in US-east / fallback options

Sara —

Thanks for the report and for engaging the on-call team. Per Neha: we can run a non-disruptive affinity-fallback that meets your request. Suggested immediate plan (60–90 minute window):

1) Approve warmup now. Neha will start the KV warmup to us-west-2. (ETA 5–8 minutes).
2) Once warmup completes we will PATCH your tenant routing to enable affinityFallback with fallbackRegions [us-west-2, eu-west-1] and graceWindowSeconds 600. This will affect new session tokens only.
3) Increase prefix TTL to 300s for 15 minutes.
4) Monitor token latency and error rate for 10 minutes; if P95 remains >1.2s we will pause and roll back.

If that sound good reply "APPROVE FALLBACK" and we'll proceed. If you prefer a single-region failover, note that automatic traffic steering to eu-west-1 may increase RTT; we recommend us-west-2 first.

Commercial note: Ben, please confirm whether VH qualifies for an SLA exception/credit should we see sustained impact after rollback.

— Marcus
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@vectorhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-oncall@vectorhealth.com, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike in US-east / fallback options

APPROVE FALLBACK — please proceed with warmup and routing change to us-west-2 first. We have the on-call team watching live metrics and will report any regression. Please send the post-action summary and full Incident Tracker link when available.

Also please include a short postmortem that explains root cause, mitigation, and steps to avoid similar host-pool hotspots. We will need this for our internal audit.

— Sara
Head of ML Platform, VectorHealth
